info.name: Future Interns - API Security Risk Analysis
info.description: Read-only API security risk assessment for Future Interns Cyber Security Task 3 (2026). Authorized public/demo APIs only. No exploitation, bypass attempts, private/production targets, or DoS/flooding.

item.name: 03 - Safe Input and API Behavior Observations

exec: pm.test('HTTP 200 response', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
pm.test('Filtered response is an array', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.be.an('array'); });
pm.test('Returned posts match requested userId', function () { pm.response.json().forEach(function (post) { pm.expect(post.userId).to.eql(1); }); });
pm.test('Documented demo login succeeds', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
pm.test('Response contains a token field', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.have.property('token'); });
pm.test('Token field is non-empty', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().token).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty; });
pm.test('Response is JSON', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type') || '').to.include('application/json'); });

request.description: Official ReqRes demo credentials for a fictitious sample account. This validates the documented login demonstration only; it does not audit a real authentication system. Do not use real personal credentials.

exec: pm.test('Missing-password request returns 400', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(400); });
pm.test('Response explains the missing password', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().error || '').to.include('Missing password'); });
pm.test('Error response is JSON', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type') || '').to.include('application/json'); });

request.description: Safe negative test documented by ReqRes: omit the password and verify the validation error. This is a normal validation example, not an attack or a finding against a production service.

exec: pm.test('List users returns HTTP 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
pm.test('Response is JSON', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type') || '').to.include('application/json'); });

pm.test('Response includes pagination metadata', function () { var body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body).to.have.property('page'); pm.expect(body).to.have.property('data'); pm.expect(body.data).to.be.an('array'); });

console.log('ReqRes observed rate-limit-related headers:', { 'ratelimit-limit': pm.response.headers.get('RateLimit-Limit'), 'ratelimit-remaining': pm.response.headers.get('RateLimit-Remaining'), 'x-ratelimit-limit': pm.response.headers.get('X-RateLimit-Limit'), 'x-ratelimit-remaining': pm.response.headers.get('X-RateLimit-Remaining'), 'retry-after': pm.response.headers.get('Retry-After') });

request.description: Documented no-key public ReqRes demo endpoint. The API documentation says the classic demo endpoints intentionally return fixed sample data; public access is by design.

exec: pm.test('Missing demo user returns HTTP 404', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(404); });
pm.test('Response is JSON', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type') || '').to.include('application/json'); });

request.description: Read-only documented not-found example. A 404 demonstrates resource-not-found handling; it does not establish an authorization failure.

item.name: 06.1 - Demo login and receive access token

exec: pm.test('Login returns HTTP 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
var body = pm.response.json();
pm.test('Response contains an accessToken', function () { pm.expect(body.accessToken).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty; });
pm.test('Response identifies the demo user', function () { pm.expect(body.username).to.eql('emilys'); });

if (body.accessToken && pm.environment) { pm.environment.set('accessToken', body.accessToken); console.log('Access token saved to the selected environment (value not printed).'); } else { console.warn('Select the Future Interns - Authentication Lab environment before running this request.'); }

request.description: Login to DummyJSON using its documented fictitious training user. The test script saves the returned access token into the masked accessToken variable in the selected Future Interns - Authentication Lab environment. Never publish the token.

exec: pm.test('Authenticated profile returns HTTP 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
pm.test('Response identifies the demo account', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().username).to.eql('emilys'); });
pm.test('Profile response does not expose password field', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).not.to.have.property('password'); });

request.description: Read-only protected endpoint. Sends the accessToken obtained by 06.1 using Authorization: Bearer. Requires the Future Interns - Authentication Lab environment selected. Do not expose the token.

exec: pm.test('Unauthenticated current-user request is rejected', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([401,403]); });
pm.test('Error response is JSON when provided', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type') || '').to.include('application/json'); });

request.description: Safe unauthenticated control test against DummyJSON's documented protected current-user endpoint. No token or credentials are sent. Expected outcome is 401/403. Record actual response.

item.name: 06.4 - Access protected profile with invalid token

exec: pm.test('Invalid token is rejected', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([401,403]); });
pm.test('Error response is JSON when provided', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type') || '').to.include('application/json'); });

request.description: Safe negative control using a deliberately invalid placeholder token against DummyJSON's documented demo authentication route. It is not a real credential. Record the actual status and error body.

item.name: 07.1 - Protected users collection with valid token

exec: pm.test('Authenticated resource request returns 2xx', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.within(200,299); });
pm.test('Response is JSON', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type') || '').to.include('application/json'); });
pm.test('Users collection is returned', function () { var body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body).to.have.property('users'); pm.expect(body.users).to.be.an('array'); });

request.description: Route-level access-control demonstration using DummyJSON's documented /auth/RESOURCE pattern. Requires the Future Interns - Authentication Lab environment and a valid masked accessToken. This is not a BOLA or role-based authorization test.

item.name: 07.2 - Observe users collection without token (200 reported)

exec: pm.test('Observed users collection request returns a success response', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.within(200,299); });
pm.test('Response is JSON with a users array', function () { var body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body).to.have.property('users'); pm.expect(body.users).to.be.an('array'); });
console.log('Observation: user reported 200 both with and without a token. This alone does not establish an access-control vulnerability.');

request.description: User-reported practical result: this route returned HTTP 200 both with and without a token. Record that observed behavior. Do not interpret it alone as BOLA/BFLA or a vulnerability because this demo endpoint's intended access policy and object ownership/role expectations were not established.

item.name: 08 - Sensitive Data Exposure and Data Minimization

exec: pm.test('Sample user request returns HTTP 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
pm.test('Response is a JSON object', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.be.an('object'); });
var u = pm.response.json();

var observed = { passwordFieldPresent: Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(u, 'password'), bankObjectPresent: !!u.bank, cardNumberFieldPresent: !!(u.bank && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(u.bank, 'cardNumber')), ibanFieldPresent: !!(u.bank && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(u.bank, 'iban')), ssnFieldPresent: Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(u, 'ssn'), cryptoWalletFieldPresent: !!(u.crypto && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(u.crypto, 'wallet')) };
console.log('Synthetic sample fields present (field names/booleans only; values not logged):', observed);
pm.test('Demo response includes one or more illustrative sensitive-like fields', function () { pm.expect(Object.values(observed).some(Boolean)).to.eql(true); });

request.description: Read-only inspection of DummyJSON's published sample user object. Its documentation deliberately shows synthetic fields such as password, bank card data, IBAN and SSN for prototyping. Treat these as fake demonstration data, not a real breach. Record only field names, never copy values into the report.

exec: pm.test('Selected-fields request returns HTTP 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
var u = pm.response.json();
pm.test('Response contains the requested basic profile fields', function () { ['id','firstName','lastName','email'].forEach(function (k) { pm.expect(u).to.have.property(k); }); });
pm.test('Response omits unrequested sensitive-like fields', function () { ['password','bank','ssn','crypto'].forEach(function (k) { pm.expect(u).not.to.have.property(k); }); });
console.log('Returned field names for data-minimization comparison:', Object.keys(u));

request.description: Demonstrates data minimization using DummyJSON's documented select query parameter. Requests only id, firstName, lastName and email. Compare the response shape with 08.1. These are synthetic demo records.

exec: pm.test('Sample products request returns a successful response', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.within(200,299); });
pm.test('Response is JSON', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type') || '').to.include('application/json'); });
var names = ['RateLimit-Limit','RateLimit-Remaining','RateLimit-Reset','X-RateLimit-Limit','X-RateLimit-Remaining','X-RateLimit-Reset','Retry-After','Cache-Control'];
var observed = {};
names.forEach(function (name) { observed[name] = pm.response.headers.get(name) || 'Not present in this response'; });
console.log('Rate-limit and cache header observations:', observed);
console.log('Response result count:', (pm.response.json().products || []).length);

request.description: Single ordinary read-only request to DummyJSON's sample products endpoint with a bounded page size (limit=10). Inspect visible rate-limit/quota and Retry-After headers if the service sends them. This does not test the enforcement threshold. Do not repeat in loops, use Collection Runner iterations, or attempt to trigger HTTP 429.

item.name: 11 - Error Handling and OWASP Risk Classification

exec: pm.test('Existing product request returns HTTP 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
pm.test('Response is a JSON object', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.be.an('object'); });
pm.test('Product object includes id and title', function () { var body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body).to.have.property('id'); pm.expect(body).to.have.property('title'); });

request.description: Read-only baseline for error-handling comparison. Request one documented sample product and inspect status, JSON error handling baseline, response body fields and timing.

exec: pm.test('Nonexistent product returns HTTP 404', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(404); });
pm.test('Error response is JSON', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type') || '').to.include('application/json'); });
var text = pm.response.text();
pm.test('Response does not expose a stack trace', function () { pm.expect(text).not.to.match(/at\s+[\w$.<>]+\s*\(|Traceback|Exception in thread|node_modules[\\/]/i); });
console.log('Observed error status:', pm.response.code, '| Response keys:', Object.keys(pm.response.json()));

request.description: Read-only check of how the demo API handles a nonexistent sample product ID. Inspect the actual status and JSON message, and check that the response does not expose a stack trace or internal server details. Do not infer a vulnerability solely from a 404.
